# Logan Eberwein

Public profile: https://loganeberwein.github.io/

Sophomore at the School of Science and Engineering (Yvonne A. Ewell Townview Center), Dallas, Texas, class of 2029. Founder of WellLens. Independent math researcher working with AI tools: a complete Lean 4 proof of Erdős Problem #1139 and a research program on the Riemann Hypothesis.

## Apps

- WellLens (September 2025 to present): fitness app that builds a workout plan from onboarding answers, with a gym buddy feature where friends send each other daily proof of their workouts. In beta on TestFlight; release planned within weeks.
- Checkback: Family Tasks: kids send photo proof of finished tasks and earn points toward rewards their parents choose. Release planned within days.

Logan directs the AI tools that write the code; he handles product decisions, design and testing.

## Erdős Problem #1139 (November 2026)

Complete Lean 4 proof of the Formal Conjectures statement erdos_1139 (answer: yes), with no sorry and only Lean's three standard axioms. Built on OpenAI's Lean formalization of "Improved Long Gaps Between Primes", with a strengthened Proposition 1.2. Liam Price posted the first (informal, GPT Pro) proof in June 2026; this is an independent route. Erdős Problem a Day rebuilt and checked it on 16 November 2026.

- Erdős Problem #1139: An Alternative Proof via Short Translates (2026). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24241059
- Code: https://github.com/loganeberwein/erdos-proofs
- Independent check: https://erdosproblemaday.com/day/1139-eberwein-lean-proof-rebuilt

## Riemann Hypothesis research (August 2025 to present)

AI-assisted work on the Riemann Hypothesis: 190 documented approaches, 297 operator candidates, Lean 4 formalization, Python computations and a public corrections log. Neither paper is a proof of RH.

- Riemann Hypothesis Research Program: Complete Progress Report and Formal Ledger (2026). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23174797
- The Truncated Weil Quadratic Form: Inertia, Visibility, Structural Measurements, and No-Go Theorems for the Riemann Hypothesis (2026). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23177438
